question: On 23 and 24 June 2022, the European Council granted Ukraine and the Republic of Moldova EU candidate country status, with accession negotiations beginning in June 2024. Georgia was granted candidate status in December 2023, before announcing on 28 November 2024 that it would be suspending its accession process until 2028.
What is more, Belarus suspended its participation in the Eastern Partnership in June 2021, while the war between Armenia and Azerbaijan has further weakened this framework.

These developments have profoundly transformed the nature of the Eastern Partnership, causing significant changes to the purpose and aims of this partnership, which seems to be at a standstill: the most recent leaders’ summit was back on 15 December 2021, and the last foreign affairs ministerial meeting took place on 11 December 2023. In view of this: 1.
Is the Commission planning a strategic review of the Eastern Partnership?
What initiatives does the Commission intend to take to relaunch high‑level political dialogue?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.6.2026) In the context of recent geopolitical developments, including Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and the EU enlargement process, the Eastern Partnership (EaP) has been adapted to ensure it remains fit for purpose. The annual EaP Senior Officials’ Meetings (SOM) constitute a key mechanism for maintaining structured political dialogue.

The latest SOM of 19 March 2026 confirmed that the EaP remains a relevant and flexible framework for regional cooperation, including in promoting the rule of law and addressing common challenges such as hybrid threats and disinformation. Connectivity, civil society and youth were also underlined as key priorities.

The Commission is taking steps to strengthen the EaP’s political dimension through ministeriallevel engagement and synergies with broader EU initiatives, such as the Strategic Approach to the Black Sea region and its flagship Connectivity Agenda1. In this context, the Commission and Member States also continue dialogue with the EaP Civil Society Forum and the EUNeighbourhood East Parliamentary Assembly2.

The Commission will continue its close cooperation with the European Parliament, Member States, and partner countries to ensure that the EaP continues to contribute to stability, prosperity, and democratic resilience in the region.
1 JOINT COMMUNICATION TO THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL The European

Union's strategic approach to the Black Sea region, JOIN/2025/135 final, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A52025JC0135&qid=1778665451529. 2 European Parliament resolution of 15 November 2007 on strengthening the European Neighbourhood Policy (2007/2088(INI)), https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-6-2007-0538_EN.html?redirect.
